Beams

Source: R/physics-continuum-beam.R
Beam.Rd

Beam(length, elastic_modulus, second_moment) is a beam bent in a plane. $apply_load(value, start, order, end) adds a load, $apply_support(loc, type) a "pin", "roller" or "fixed" support and $apply_rotation_hinge() and $apply_sliding_hinge() hinges; $solve_for_reaction_loads() finds the reactions. $shear_force(), $bending_moment(), $slope(), $deflection() and $shear_stress() give the curves along the beam, $max_shear_force(), $max_bmoment(), $max_deflection() and $point_cflexure() their extremes, and $solve_for_ild_reactions(), $solve_for_ild_shear() and $solve_for_ild_moment() the influence lines. The boundary conditions are $bc_deflection, $bc_slope, $bc_bending_moment and $bc_shear_force. $join() joins two beams. The $plot_*() methods draw base R plots. Beam3D(length, elastic_modulus, shear_modulus, second_moment, area) is a beam loaded in three dimensions. After sympy.physics.continuum_mechanics.beam.

Usage

Beam(
  length,
  elastic_modulus,
  second_moment,
  area = Symbol("A"),
  variable = Symbol("x"),
  base_char = "C",
  ild_variable = Symbol("a")
)

Beam3D(
  length,
  elastic_modulus,
  shear_modulus,
  second_moment,
  area,
  variable = Symbol("x")
)

Arguments

length, elastic_modulus

The length and the elastic modulus.

second_moment

The second moment of area, or a geometry entity giving the cross section.

area

The cross section area.

variable

The coordinate along the beam.

base_char

The base name of the integration constants.

ild_variable

The position of the moving load of the influence lines.

shear_modulus

The shear modulus.

Value

A Beam or Beam3D object.

Examples

E <- Symbol("E"); I <- Symbol("I")
b <- Beam(30, E, I)
R1 <- b$apply_support(10, "roller"); R2 <- b$apply_support(30, "roller")
b$apply_load(-8, 0, -1)
b$solve_for_reaction_loads(R1, R2)
b$reaction_loads
#> {R_10: 12, R_30: -4} 
b$bending_moment()
#> 8*SingularityFunction(x, 0, 1) - 12*SingularityFunction(x, 10, 1) + 4*SingularityFunction(x, 30, 1)
